components.note: 乛 (hook stroke) — the top-left bent stroke and dictionary radical; a stroke grouping with no meaning of its own.
一 (one) — the bottom bar. 卫 is simplified from 衛 (guard); Memory aid: a bar blocking a corner, a guard at the door.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 医生建议大家勤洗手，注意卫生。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì dàjiā qín xǐshǒu, zhùyì wèishēng.
example.english: Doctors recommend that everyone wash their hands often and pay attention to hygiene.
example.fact: In the 1840s, Hungarian doctor Ignaz Semmelweis found that having physicians wash their hands with chlorinated lime before delivering babies cut maternal deaths from childbed fever by nearly 90 percent. His colleagues largely rejected the idea at the time, and it was only decades later, after the acceptance of germ theory, that his work was recognized as a major breakthrough in hygiene.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的卫生做得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de wèishēng zuò de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This restaurant keeps very good hygiene.

examples.hanzi: 请大家一起打扫卫生。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā yìqǐ dǎsǎo wèishēng.
examples.english: Everyone, please clean up together.

components.note: 夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.
女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.

example.hanzi: 这是她的处女作，一经出版就受到广泛好评。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì tā de chǔnǚzuò, yìjīng chūbǎn jiù shòudào guǎngfàn hǎopíng.
example.english: This is her debut work, and it received widespread praise as soon as it was published.
example.fact: The Virgin Islands were named by Christopher Columbus in 1493 after Saint Ursula and her legendary eleven thousand virgin companions, a story from medieval Christian folklore, apparently because the sheer number of islands and islets he encountered reminded him of the huge legendary retinue.

examples.hanzi: 这是这位作家的处女作。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zhè wèi zuòjiā de chǔnǚzuò.
examples.english: This is the writer's first work.

examples.hanzi: 这艘船要进行处女航。
examples.pinyin: Zhè sōu chuán yào jìnxíng chǔnǚháng.
examples.english: This ship is about to make its maiden voyage.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 陷 is falling into a pit.
臽 (xiàn) — same sound — 陷 is xiàn; 臽 also sounds out 馅 xiàn.

example.hanzi: 汽车陷在泥里了。
example.pinyin: Qìchē xiàn zài ní lǐ le.
example.english: The car is stuck in the mud.
example.fact: 陷 means falling or sinking into a hole: 陷入 (to fall into), 陷阱 (trap), 缺陷 (defect), 沦陷 (to fall to an enemy). 陷害 means to frame someone.

examples.hanzi: 他不小心陷进了泥坑里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn xiàn jìn le níkēng lǐ.
examples.english: He accidentally sank into a mud pit.

examples.hanzi: 这个计划有一个缺陷。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà yǒu yí ge quēxiàn.
examples.english: This plan has a flaw.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.hanzi: 图书馆里，大家都小声说话。
example.pinyin: Túshūguǎn lǐ, dàjiā dōu xiǎoshēng shuōhuà.
example.english: In the library, everyone speaks in a low voice.
example.fact: The convention of near-total silence in libraries is a fairly modern one, taking hold mostly in the 19th and 20th centuries. The ancient Library of Alexandria, one of the largest libraries of the classical world, is believed to have functioned as a lively center of scholarly debate rather than a hushed reading room.

examples.hanzi: 宝宝睡着了，请小声一点。
examples.pinyin: Bǎobao shuìzháo le, qǐng xiǎoshēng yìdiǎn.
examples.english: The baby is asleep, so please keep your voice down.

examples.hanzi: 他小声地对我说了一个秘密。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎoshēng de duì wǒ shuō le yí ge mìmì.
examples.english: He quietly told me a secret.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
攵 (tap, strike) — marks actions, as in 教, 改, 放; 散 is to scatter (sàn) or to be loose (sǎn).

example.hanzi: 蒲公英的种子靠风分散到很远的地方。
example.pinyin: Púgōngyīng de zhǒngzi kào fēng fēnsàn dào hěn yuǎn de dìfāng.
example.english: Dandelion seeds are scattered far away by the wind.
example.fact: In 2018, researchers at the University of Edinburgh discovered that each dandelion seed's fluffy tuft creates a stable, ring-shaped vortex of air above it as it falls, a structure never seen before in nature. This 'separated vortex ring' is about four times more efficient at generating drag than a parachute of similar size, letting the tiny seed travel over a kilometer on the wind.

examples.hanzi: 大雾把人们的注意力分散了。
examples.pinyin: Dàwù bǎ rénmen de zhùyìlì fēnsàn le.
examples.english: The fog distracted people's attention.

examples.hanzi: 一下课，同学们就分散到了操场上。
examples.pinyin: Yí xiàkè, tóngxuémen jiù fēnsàn dào le cāochǎng shàng.
examples.english: As soon as class ended, the students scattered across the playground.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 这家博物馆全年向公众开放。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā bówùguǎn quánnián xiàng gōngzhòng kāifàng.
example.english: This museum is open to the public all year round.
example.fact: The Louvre in Paris, now the world's most-visited museum, first opened its doors to the public in 1793 during the French Revolution, turning a former royal palace into a place where ordinary citizens, not just nobility, could view its art collection.

examples.hanzi: 春天公园里的樱花全部开放了。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān gōngyuán lǐ de yīnghuā quánbù kāifàng le.
examples.english: In spring, all the cherry blossoms in the park are in bloom.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家决定对外开放市场。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā juédìng duìwài kāifàng shìchǎng.
examples.english: This country decided to open up its market to the outside world.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 他老是忘记带钥匙。
example.pinyin: Tā lǎoshi wàngjì dài yàoshi.
example.english: He is always forgetting to bring his keys.
example.fact: German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus described the 'forgetting curve' in 1885 after testing his own memory with nonsense syllables, finding that without any review, people forget roughly half of newly learned information within about an hour and up to 70 percent within a day. His work became a founding study in memory research.

examples.hanzi: 你怎么老是迟到？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme lǎoshi chídào?
examples.english: Why are you always late?

examples.hanzi: 他老是问同样的问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā lǎoshi wèn tóngyàng de wèntí.
examples.english: He keeps asking the same question.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之) — marks movement and roads, as in 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; 逛 is strolling around.
狂 (kuáng) — close sound: 逛 guàng. 狂 also sounds out 诳 kuáng.

example.hanzi: 周末我们去商场逛逛吧。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù shāngchǎng guàngguang ba.
example.english: Let's go stroll around the mall this weekend.
example.fact: 逛街 means strolling and window-shopping without any need to buy anything, which English cannot capture in one word. It now extends to online browsing: 逛淘宝 (browsing Taobao).

examples.hanzi: 你想不想陪我去逛街？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng bu xiǎng péi wǒ qù guàngjiē?
examples.english: Do you want to go shopping with me?

examples.hanzi: 我们在公园里逛了一个下午。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài gōngyuán lǐ guàng le yí ge xiàwǔ.
examples.english: We strolled around the park all afternoon.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth, as in 地, 城; a mold was made of clay, so 型 is a model or type.
刑 (xíng) — same sound — 型 is xíng, like 刑.

example.hanzi: 这座城市正在建设一座大型体育馆。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì zhèngzài jiànshè yí zuò dàxíng tǐyùguǎn.
example.english: This city is building a large-scale stadium.
example.fact: North Korea's Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang is the largest stadium in the world by capacity, seating around 114,000 spectators. It is used mainly for the Arirang Mass Games, a large-scale synchronized gymnastics and artistic performance involving tens of thousands of participants.

examples.hanzi: 这是一场大型音乐会。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yì chǎng dàxíng yīnyuèhuì.
examples.english: This is a large-scale concert.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司买了一台大型机器。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī mǎi le yì tái dàxíng jīqì.
examples.english: This company bought a large machine.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions done by hand, as in 找 look for, 拿 take, 抓 grab; 搜 is to search by hand.
叟 (sǒu) — same sound family — 搜 is sōu; 叟 also sounds out 艘 sōu.
寸 (inch, hand) — measuring and hands: 对, 导, 寺; 寻 traditionally meant stretching arms to measure, then searching.

example.hanzi: 救援队连夜搜寻失踪的登山者。
example.pinyin: Jiùyuánduì liányè sōuxún shīzōng de dēngshānzhě.
example.english: The rescue team searched through the night for the missing climber.
example.fact: The SETI project has used radio telescopes since 1960 to search the sky for signals from other civilizations. Its most famous find, the 1977 'Wow! signal' picked up by Ohio State University's Big Ear telescope, remains an unexplained 72-second burst that has never been detected again.

examples.hanzi: 我在房间里到处搜寻丢掉的钥匙。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài fángjiān lǐ dàochù sōuxún diūdiào de yàoshi.
examples.english: I searched everywhere in the room for my lost keys.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在搜寻线索。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài sōuxún xiànsuǒ.
examples.english: The police are looking for clues.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 is the heart, as in 想, 思, 念; 忍 is a blade 刃 over the heart — enduring pain.
刃 (rèn) — near sound — 忍 is rěn; 刃 is a blade with an edge marked by a dot.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 看到这么好笑的视频，她忍不住笑了出来。
example.pinyin: Kàndào zhème hǎoxiào de shìpín, tā rěnbuzhù xiàole chūlái.
example.english: Seeing such a funny video, she couldn't help but laugh.
example.fact: Laughter is famously contagious, a phenomenon linked to mirror neurons that fire both when we act and when we watch someone else act. American sound engineer Charley Douglass exploited this in 1950 by building the 'laff box,' a device used to add pre-recorded laugh tracks to sitcoms, a technique that shaped decades of American television comedy.

examples.hanzi: 听到这个好消息，我忍不住哭了。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège hǎo xiāoxi, wǒ rěn bu zhù kū le.
examples.english: Hearing the good news, I couldn't help crying.

examples.hanzi: 蛋糕太香了，我忍不住想多吃一块。
examples.pinyin: Dàngāo tài xiāng le, wǒ rěn bu zhù xiǎng duō chī yí kuài.
examples.english: The cake smells so good that I can't help wanting another piece.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound) — as in 险, 阳, 阴: a walled yard.
完 (wán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; also in 玩 wán.

example.hanzi: 他因为高烧不退，被送去住院观察。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi gāoshāo bú tuì, bèi sòng qù zhùyuàn guānchá.
example.english: Because his fever wouldn't go down, he was sent to the hospital for observation.
example.fact: The bimaristans of the medieval Islamic world, some dating to 9th-century Baghdad, are considered among the earliest hospitals with organized wards for different illnesses and rotating medical staff. Patients being discharged were sometimes given a small sum of money to help cover their recovery period.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶上周住院了，我们都去看她。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai shàngzhōu zhùyuàn le, wǒmen dōu qù kàn tā.
examples.english: Grandma was hospitalized last week, and we all went to see her.

examples.hanzi: 他住院三天就出院了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhùyuàn sān tiān jiù chūyuàn le.
examples.english: He was discharged after staying in the hospital for three days.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and washing, as in 洗 wash, 游 swim, 洗澡; 浴 is a bath.
谷 (yù/gǔ) gives the sound: 浴 yù, also in 欲 yù and 裕 yù.
缶 (earthenware jar) — pottery vessels, as in 罐 jar, 缺 lack; 缸 is a crock or vat.
工 (gōng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 红 hóng and 江 jiāng.

example.hanzi: 她放了满满一浴缸热水，准备泡澡。
example.pinyin: Tā fàngle mǎnmǎn yī yùgāng rè shuǐ, zhǔnbèi pàozǎo.
example.english: She filled the bathtub full of hot water, ready to soak.
example.fact: According to legend, the Greek mathematician Archimedes discovered the principle of buoyancy around 250 BC while stepping into a filled bathtub, noticing the water level rise and realizing an object's volume could be measured by the water it displaced. He supposedly shouted 'Eureka!' and ran through the streets of Syracuse still dripping wet.

examples.hanzi: 我们家的浴缸太小了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā de yùgāng tài xiǎo le.
examples.english: The bathtub in our home is too small.

examples.hanzi: 她躺在浴缸里听音乐。
examples.pinyin: Tā tǎng zài yùgāng lǐ tīng yīnyuè.
examples.english: She lies in the bathtub listening to music.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — jewels and polished things: 玩, 现, 理, 玻; 球 first meant a round gem.
求 (qiú) sounds exactly like 球.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 孩子们放学后常在球场上打篮球。
example.pinyin: Háizimen fàngxué hòu cháng zài qiúchǎng shàng dǎ lánqiú.
example.english: After school, the children often play basketball on the court.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in 1891 by Canadian-American physical education instructor James Naismith, who nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony at a Massachusetts YMCA to serve as goals. Because the baskets still had their bottoms, someone had to fetch a ladder to retrieve the ball after every single score.

examples.hanzi: 球场上的灯光太亮了。
examples.pinyin: Qiúchǎng shàng de dēngguāng tài liàng le.
examples.english: The lights on the field are very bright.

examples.hanzi: 我们周末约好去球场踢球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò yuē hǎo qù qiúchǎng tīqiú.
examples.english: We agreed to go play soccer on the field this weekend.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们; 何 was a person carrying a load (荷 hè).
可 (kě) is a close sound clue for hé; also in 河 hé, 歌 gē and 哥 gē.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.

example.hanzi: 天气这么好，我们何不去公园散步呢？
example.pinyin: Tiānqì zhème hǎo, wǒmen hébù qù gōngyuán sànbù ne?
example.english: The weather is so nice, why don't we go for a walk in the park?
example.fact: New York's Central Park, designed in 1858 by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux, was entirely man-made and required more blasting powder to remove its rocky terrain than was used at the Battle of Gettysburg five years later. It remains one of the most visited urban parks in the world.

examples.hanzi: 你饿了，何不先吃点东西？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ è le, hébù xiān chī diǎn dōngxi?
examples.english: You're hungry, so why not eat something first?

examples.hanzi: 遇到问题，何不问问老师？
examples.pinyin: Yùdào wèntí, hébù wènwen lǎoshī?
examples.english: When you have a problem, why not ask the teacher?

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 说 say, 问 ask; 告 is "to tell". 告 also gives sound to 造 zào and 靠 kào.
口 (mouth) — knowing is something you can say aloud; 口 sits in many speech words (问 ask, 告 tell).
矢 (shǐ, arrow) is only a loose sound clue today; the same 知 sound is in 智 zhì (wisdom).

example.hanzi: 学校已经告知家长明天放假的消息。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào yǐjīng gàozhī jiāzhǎng míngtiān fàngjià de xiāoxi.
example.english: The school has already informed parents that there's no class tomorrow.
example.fact: The Pony Express, running from 1860 to 1861 in the United States, relayed messages nearly 2,900 kilometers from Missouri to California in about ten days using riders who swapped horses at stations roughly every 16 kilometers, cutting delivery time from weeks to days before it was made obsolete within two years by the transcontinental telegraph.

examples.hanzi: 请及时告知我你的决定。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jíshí gàozhī wǒ nǐ de juédìng.
examples.english: Please let me know your decision in time.

examples.hanzi: 医生已经告知他检查结果。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng yǐjīng gàozhī tā jiǎnchá jiéguǒ.
examples.english: The doctor has already informed him of the test results.

components.note: 冫 (ice, 两点水) — marks cold and freezing, as in 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 决; 冻 is freezing.
东 (dōng) — close sound: 冻 dòng. 东 also sounds out 栋 dòng and 动 dòng.

example.hanzi: 外面太冷了，我的手都冻僵了。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài lěng le, wǒ de shǒu dōu dòngjiāng le.
example.english: It is so cold outside that my hands are frozen stiff.
example.fact: 冻 can mean frozen water, as in 冰冻, or to feel painfully cold: 冻死我了 (I'm freezing). Also 冷冻 (frozen food), 冻结 (to freeze assets) and 果冻 (jelly).

examples.hanzi: 冬天湖水会冻起来。
examples.pinyin: Dōngtiān húshuǐ huì dòng qǐlái.
examples.english: The lake freezes in winter.

examples.hanzi: 我把肉放在冰箱里冻着。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ ròu fàng zài bīngxiāng lǐ dòng zhe.
examples.english: I keep the meat frozen in the fridge.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 老师指出了这篇作文中的几个错误。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhǐchūle zhè piān zuòwén zhōng de jǐ gè cuòwù.
example.english: The teacher pointed out several mistakes in this essay.
example.fact: In 1912, meteorologist Alfred Wegener pointed out that the coastlines of Africa and South America fit together like puzzle pieces and proposed the theory of continental drift. Most geologists dismissed the idea at the time, and it was not until the 1960s, with the discovery of plate tectonics, that his theory was confirmed.

examples.hanzi: 他指出了我们计划中的问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǐchū le wǒmen jìhuà zhōng de wèntí.
examples.english: He pointed out the problems in our plan.

examples.hanzi: 请你指出地图上的位置。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zhǐchū dìtú shàng de wèizhi.
examples.english: Please point out the location on the map.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads, as in 道 road, 过 pass, 进 enter.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 迪克是我们班上跑得最快的同学。
example.pinyin: Díkè shì wǒmen bān shàng pǎo de zuì kuài de tóngxué.
example.english: Dick is the fastest runner in our class.
example.fact: American high jumper Dick Fosbury revolutionized his sport at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics by going over the bar backwards and headfirst instead of using the traditional straddle technique. His unconventional 'Fosbury Flop' won him a gold medal and is now used by nearly every elite high jumper in the world.

examples.hanzi: 迪克明天要去学校参加比赛。
examples.pinyin: Díkè míngtiān yào qù xuéxiào cānjiā bǐsài.
examples.english: Dick is going to school tomorrow to take part in a competition.

examples.hanzi: 我把书借给了迪克。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shū jiè gěi le Díkè.
examples.english: I lent the book to Dick.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 咋 is a dialect question word, how or why.
乍 (zhà) — close sound: 咋 zǎ. 乍 also sounds out 诈 zhà and 炸 zhà.

example.hanzi: 你咋还不回家？
example.pinyin: Nǐ zǎ hái bù huí jiā?
example.english: How come you are still not going home?
example.fact: 咋 is a northern colloquial form of 怎么: 咋办 (what to do), 咋样 (how is it). Another reading zé appears in 咋舌 (to be astonished into silence).

examples.hanzi: 你咋不早点告诉我？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zǎ bù zǎodiǎn gàosu wǒ?
examples.english: Why didn't you tell me earlier?

examples.hanzi: 这事儿咋办呀？
examples.pinyin: Zhè shìr zǎ bàn ya?
examples.english: What should we do about this?

components.note: 土 (earth) — a mound of earth; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
文 (wén) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 蚊 wén and 纹 wén.
土 (earth) — a burial in the ground; also in 地 ground, 城 city.
莫 (mò) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 幕 mù, 慕 mù and 募 mù.

example.hanzi: 考古学家在这座坟墓中发现了许多陪葬品。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài zhè zuò fénmù zhōng fāxiànle xǔduō péizàngpǐn.
example.english: Archaeologists discovered many burial artifacts in this tomb.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, buried near the tomb of China's first emperor Qin Shi Huang around 210 BC, contains over 8,000 life-sized clay soldiers, each with individually sculpted facial features. It was discovered entirely by accident in 1974 by farmers digging a well.

examples.hanzi: 清明节，我们去给祖先的坟墓扫墓。
examples.pinyin: Qīngmíngjié, wǒmen qù gěi zǔxiān de fénmù sǎomù.
examples.english: On Qingming Festival, we visit our ancestors' graves.

examples.hanzi: 山坡上有一座古老的坟墓。
examples.pinyin: Shānpō shàng yǒu yí zuò gǔlǎo de fénmù.
examples.english: There is an ancient tomb on the hillside.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes, as in 阶 steps, 院, 陆; 降 is to go down a slope.
夅 (two feet going down) — shows descent, and gives the sound: 降 jiàng.
临 (simplified 臨) — the old form shows a person bending over with a watching eye above a heap of goods: looking down on something, hence 'to face, to draw near'.

example.hanzi: 夜幕降临，城市的灯光渐渐亮了起来。
example.pinyin: Yèmù jiànglín, chéngshì de dēngguāng jiànjiàn liàngle qǐlái.
example.english: As night fell, the city lights gradually came on.
example.fact: A total solar eclipse creates an eerie sudden darkness called 'totality,' which can drop nearby temperatures several degrees within minutes and confuse animal behavior — birds often fall silent and nocturnal creatures begin to stir. This was well documented across North America during the total eclipse of April 2024.

examples.hanzi: 春天降临了，大地变绿了。
examples.pinyin: Chūntiān jiànglín le, dàdì biàn lǜ le.
examples.english: Spring has arrived and the land has turned green.

examples.hanzi: 黑夜降临，大家回到了帐篷里。
examples.pinyin: Hēiyè jiànglín, dàjiā huí dào le zhàngpeng lǐ.
examples.english: Night fell, and everyone returned to the tent.

components.note: 文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 古埃及是人类历史上最早的文明之一。
example.pinyin: Gǔ Āijí shì rénlèi lìshǐ shàng zuìzǎo de wénmíng zhī yī.
example.english: Ancient Egypt is one of the earliest civilizations in human history.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptian civilization thrived along the Nile for more than 3,000 years, and its calendar, based on the river's predictable annual flooding, divided the year into 365 days — a system remarkably close to the calendar most of the world still uses today.

examples.hanzi: 中国有悠久的历史和灿烂的文明。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒu yōujiǔ de lìshǐ hé cànlàn de wénmíng.
examples.english: China has a long history and a splendid civilization.

examples.hanzi: 请文明使用公共设施。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng wénmíng shǐyòng gōnggòng shèshī.
examples.english: Please use public facilities in a civilized manner.

meanings: official (approved or issued by an authority)

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.

example.hanzi: 政府发布了官方声明，澄清了这一事件。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ fābùle guānfāng shēngmíng, chéngqīngle zhè yī shìjiàn.
example.english: The government issued an official statement clarifying the incident.
example.fact: The Behistun Inscription, carved around 500 BC into a cliff in present-day Iran on the order of Persian King Darius I, is one of the oldest known official proclamations, written in three languages. Its trilingual text later became the key that let scholars decipher cuneiform script, much as the Rosetta Stone did for Egyptian hieroglyphs.

examples.hanzi: 这是官方网站发布的消息。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì guānfāng wǎngzhàn fābù de xiāoxi.
examples.english: This is news released by the official website.

examples.hanzi: 官方还没有公布比赛的结果。
examples.pinyin: Guānfāng hái méiyǒu gōngbù bǐsài de jiéguǒ.
examples.english: The authorities have not yet announced the match results.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住; 候 means to wait for someone.
侯 (hóu) is a close sound clue for hòu; it also gives 猴 hóu monkey and 喉 hóu throat.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 三位候选人将在明天的选举中角逐市长职位。
example.pinyin: Sān wèi hòuxuǎnrén jiāng zài míngtiān de xuǎnjǔ zhōng juézhú shìzhǎng zhíwèi.
example.english: Three candidates will compete for the mayoral position in tomorrow's election.
example.fact: Ancient Athens practiced ostracism, in which citizens could vote to exile a person for ten years by scratching their name onto a broken piece of pottery called an ostrakon. Thousands of these inscribed shards have survived, giving historians a direct record of which political candidates and figures were unpopular over 2,400 years ago.

examples.hanzi: 每位候选人都要发表演讲。
examples.pinyin: Měi wèi hòuxuǎnrén dōu yào fābiǎo yǎnjiǎng.
examples.english: Each candidate has to give a speech.

examples.hanzi: 她是班长的候选人之一。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì bānzhǎng de hòuxuǎnrén zhī yī.
examples.english: She is one of the candidates for class monitor.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — 夕 is evening or dusk, as in 外, 多, 梦; 夜 is night.
亦 (yì) — near sound — 夜 is yè; 夜 also sounds out 液 yè.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 总 is simplified from 總, whose threads gathered everything together.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 这家夜总会每天晚上都有现场音乐表演。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yèzǒnghuì měitiān wǎnshàng dōu yǒu xiànchǎng yīnyuè biǎoyǎn.
example.english: This nightclub has live music performances every night.
example.fact: Studio 54 in New York City operated for less than a decade, from 1977 to 1986, but became one of the most famous nightclubs in history thanks to its strict door policy and star-studded crowds. Its brief run left a lasting influence on nightlife culture worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 他们晚上去夜总会听歌。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen wǎnshang qù yèzǒnghuì tīng gē.
examples.english: They go to a nightclub in the evening to listen to music.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市的夜总会很热闹。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì de yèzǒnghuì hěn rènao.
examples.english: The nightclubs in this city are very lively.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 力 marks strength and effort, as in 办, 动, 努, 助; 勇 is strength in action, courage.
甬 (yǒng) — same sound — 勇 is yǒng, like 甬; 甬 also sounds out 通 tōng, 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 古代的武士以勇士的精神著称。
example.pinyin: Gǔdài de wǔshì yǐ yǒngshì de jīngshén zhùchēng.
example.english: Ancient warriors were known for their warrior spirit.
example.fact: Japan's samurai followed a code known as bushido, 'the way of the warrior,' which emphasized loyalty, honor, and discipline. The samurai class was formally abolished in 1876 during the Meiji Restoration as Japan replaced its warrior aristocracy with a modern conscript army.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位勇敢的勇士。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi yǒnggǎn de yǒngshì.
examples.english: He is a brave warrior.

examples.hanzi: 电影里的勇士打败了怪兽。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de yǒngshì dǎbài le guàishòu.
examples.english: The warrior in the movie defeated the monster.

components.note: 牙 (tooth) — a picture of interlocking teeth; 牙 also sounds out 芽 yá and 讶 yà.
医 (doctor) — simplified from 醫, which had 酉 (medicinal wine, as in 酒) at the bottom; the box 匚 and arrow 矢 remain.

example.hanzi: 牙医建议我每半年做一次牙齿检查。
example.pinyin: Yáyī jiànyì wǒ měi bàn nián zuò yí cì yáchǐ jiǎnchá.
example.english: The dentist recommended I have a dental checkup every six months.
example.fact: The oldest known dental filling was found in a 13,000-year-old tooth in Italy, where prehistoric people packed a cavity with bitumen mixed with plant fibers and hair. It shows that basic dental care predates written history by thousands of years.

examples.hanzi: 我明天下午要去看牙医。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān xiàwǔ yào qù kàn yáyī.
examples.english: I'm going to see the dentist tomorrow afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 牙医告诉我不要吃太多糖。
examples.pinyin: Yáyī gàosu wǒ bú yào chī tài duō táng.
examples.english: The dentist told me not to eat too much sugar.

components.note: 三 — three strokes, one more than 二. The numbers 一 二 三 are the only ones counted by drawing lines.
十 (ten) — a cross: first a single vertical line, later crossed with a horizontal bar. Seen in 十分, 二十, and in 千.

example.hanzi: 她今年三十岁，是公司里最年轻的经理。
example.pinyin: Tā jīnnián sānshí suì, shì gōngsī lǐ zuì niánqīng de jīnglǐ.
example.english: She is thirty years old this year, the youngest manager in the company.
example.fact: The Moon takes about 29.5 days to complete a full cycle of phases, which is close to thirty — a coincidence that led many ancient calendars, including the Babylonian and early Chinese lunar calendars, to build their months around roughly thirty-day cycles.

examples.hanzi: 我们班有三十个学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān yǒu sānshí ge xuésheng.
examples.english: There are thirty students in our class.

examples.hanzi: 三十分钟以后，我们在门口见。
examples.pinyin: Sānshí fēnzhōng yǐhòu, wǒmen zài ménkǒu jiàn.
examples.english: Let's meet at the entrance in thirty minutes.

components.note: 木 (wood) — palm trees; also in 树 tree, 林 forest.
宗 (zōng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 踪 zōng and 综 zōng.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 秋天的树叶渐渐变成了棕色。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān de shùyè jiànjiàn biànchéngle zōngsè.
example.english: Autumn leaves gradually turned brown.
example.fact: Leaves turn brown, yellow, or orange in autumn because chlorophyll, the green pigment used for photosynthesis, breaks down as daylight shortens. This reveals carotenoid pigments that were present in the leaf all along but had been masked by green throughout the summer.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢棕色的皮鞋。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan zōngsè de píxié.
examples.english: I like brown leather shoes the most.

examples.hanzi: 这只小狗有棕色的眼睛。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎogǒu yǒu zōngsè de yǎnjing.
examples.english: This puppy has brown eyes.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 推 is to push.
隹 (zhuī) is a loose hint for tuī; 堆 duī and 谁 shéi share it.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 深, 浅; 测 was measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) is close to cè; same part in 侧 cè and 厕 cè.

example.hanzi: 天文学家推测这颗行星上可能存在液态水。
example.pinyin: Tiānwénxuéjiā tuīcè zhè kē xíngxīng shàng kěnéng cúnzài yètài shuǐ.
example.english: Astronomers speculate that this planet may have liquid water.
example.fact: Europa, one of Jupiter's moons, is thought to hide a liquid water ocean beneath its icy crust that may contain roughly twice the volume of water in all of Earth's oceans combined. That makes it one of the leading candidates in the solar system for finding microbial life beyond Earth.

examples.hanzi: 专家推测明年的价格会下降。
examples.pinyin: Zhuānjiā tuīcè míngnián de jiàgé huì xiàjiàng.
examples.english: Experts speculate that prices will fall next year.

examples.hanzi: 根据地上的脚印，他推测有人来过。
examples.pinyin: Gēnjù dìshàng de jiǎoyìn, tā tuīcè yǒu rén lái guo.
examples.english: Judging from the footprints, he inferred that someone had been there.

meanings: to go so far as to

components.note: 音 (sound) — a piece of music 音 played to its end by a person 儿: finishing, then "at last" or unexpectedly.

example.hanzi: 他竟然忘了自己的生日。
example.pinyin: Tā jìngrán wàng le zìjǐ de shēngrì.
example.english: He actually forgot his own birthday.
example.fact: 竟 expresses surprise and usually appears as 竟然. It is close to 居然, with 竟 a bit more written. Its older meaning is "to finish," kept in 终竟 and 究竟 (after all), 毕竟 (after all).

examples.hanzi: 我竟然在街上遇到了老同学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jìngrán zài jiē shàng yùdào le lǎo tóngxué.
examples.english: I unexpectedly ran into an old classmate on the street.

examples.hanzi: 他竟敢一个人去爬那座高山。
examples.pinyin: Tā jìng gǎn yí ge rén qù pá nà zuò gāoshān.
examples.english: He actually dared to climb that mountain alone.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室, 安; 宗 is the ancestral hall.
示 (altar) — 示 is an altar to the ancestors — a house with an altar means clan and religion.

example.hanzi: 这个宗教有很长的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhège zōngjiào yǒu hěn cháng de lìshǐ.
example.english: This religion has a long history.
example.fact: 宗 is rooted in ancestor worship: 祖宗 (ancestors), 宗族 (clan), and then 宗教 (religion), 宗旨 (aim). As a measure word it counts cases or goods: 一宗案件, 大宗货物 (bulk goods).

examples.hanzi: 他的宗教信仰很特别。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zōngjiào xìnyǎng hěn tèbié.
examples.english: His religious belief is very special.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事讲的是家族的祖宗。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi jiǎng de shì jiāzú de zǔzong.
examples.english: This story is about the ancestors of a family.

components.note: 日 (sun) — marks sun, daylight and time, as in 明 bright, 晚 evening, 早 early; 晒 is drying or basking in the sun.
西 (xī) — loose sound hint (shài vs xī); same part in 洒 sǎ.

example.hanzi: 他把被子拿到外面晒太阳。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ bèizi ná dào wàimiàn shài tàiyáng.
example.english: He took the quilt outside to air in the sun.
example.fact: 晒太阳 (to bask in the sun) is a common wish for relaxation and health; 晒被子 means airing bedding; 晒伤 is sunburn. Online, 晒 means to show off something publicly: 晒照片, 晒工资.

examples.hanzi: 天气好，我们去晒太阳吧。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì hǎo, wǒmen qù shài tàiyáng ba.
examples.english: The weather is nice, so let's go bask in the sun.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢在网上晒自己的照片。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài wǎng shàng shài zìjǐ de zhàopiàn.
examples.english: She likes to post her photos online.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; 审 is a hearing held in a hall.
申 (shēn) is a near sound match for shěn; also in 神 shén, 伸 shēn.
门 (mén, gate) is a close sound clue for wèn; the picture is asking at a gate, as in 闻 wén.
口 (mouth) — speaking, as in 吃, 唱, 叫: asking is a mouth action.

example.hanzi: 警察对嫌疑人进行了长时间的审问。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá duì xiányírén jìnxíngle cháng shíjiān de shěnwèn.
example.english: The police interrogated the suspect for a long time.
example.fact: The polygraph, popularly known as a 'lie detector,' was developed in the 1920s by American police officer John Larson, but its scientific validity remains disputed. The American Psychological Association notes there is no evidence any single physiological pattern is uniquely tied to lying, which is why most courts do not accept polygraph results as reliable evidence.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在审问那个嫌疑人。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài shěnwèn nàge xiányírén.
examples.english: The police are questioning that suspect.

examples.hanzi: 他被审问了整整一个下午。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi shěnwèn le zhěngzhěng yí ge xiàwǔ.
examples.english: He was interrogated for the whole afternoon.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — ships, as in 船 ship, 航 sail.
见 (jiàn) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 览 lǎn and 现 xiàn loosely.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 这支舰队将在下周展开一次联合军事演习。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī jiànduì jiāng zài xià zhōu zhǎnkāi yí cì liánhé jūnshì yǎnxí.
example.english: This fleet will conduct a joint military exercise next week.
example.fact: The Spanish Armada of 1588, sent by King Philip II to invade England with about 130 ships, was ultimately defeated by a mix of English naval tactics and a violent storm that scattered the fleet along the coasts of Scotland and Ireland, sinking dozens of vessels.

examples.hanzi: 一支舰队驶入了港口。
examples.pinyin: Yì zhī jiànduì shǐ rù le gǎngkǒu.
examples.english: A fleet sailed into the harbor.

examples.hanzi: 这支舰队有二十多艘船。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī jiànduì yǒu èrshí duō sōu chuán.
examples.english: This fleet has more than twenty ships.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; counting aloud.
十 (ten) — counting up to ten: 计 is to count and reckon.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔 pen, 等 wait, 第: counting rods were once bamboo.
具 (jù, tool) — here the lower part shows hands holding the counting tools.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 世界上第一台电子计算机诞生于1946年。
example.pinyin: Shìjiè shàng dì yī tái diànzǐ jìsuànjī dànshēng yú yījiǔsìliù nián.
example.english: The world's first electronic computer was born in 1946.
example.fact: ENIAC, completed in 1945 and publicly unveiled in 1946, is often described as the first general-purpose electronic computer. It weighed about 30 tons, filled an entire room, and relied on nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes, which failed so frequently that technicians typically had to replace one almost every day.

examples.hanzi: 我的计算机坏了，需要修理。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jìsuànjī huài le, xūyào xiūlǐ.
examples.english: My computer is broken and needs repair.

examples.hanzi: 他在大学里学习计算机。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué lǐ xuéxí jìsuànjī.
examples.english: He studies computer science at university.

components.note: 曲 (bent) — the shape pictures something bent; qū means crooked and qǔ means a song, as in 歌曲.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 她哼着一首熟悉的曲子走进了房间。
example.pinyin: Tā hēngzhe yì shǒu shúxī de qǔzi zǒujìnle fángjiān.
example.english: Humming a familiar tune, she walked into the room.
example.fact: The Seikilos Epitaph, a Greek tune carved onto a marble column in what is now Turkey around the 1st or 2nd century AD, is the oldest complete piece of music known to survive from antiquity, preserving both its lyrics and specific melodic notation.

examples.hanzi: 这首曲子听起来很轻松。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu qǔzi tīng qǐlái hěn qīngsōng.
examples.english: This tune sounds very relaxing.

examples.hanzi: 你会弹这支曲子吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì tán zhè zhī qǔzi ma?
examples.english: Can you play this piece?

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
方 (square; flag) — stands in for the flag part 㫃 of the old form, as in 旗 flag, 旅 travel, 族 clan; the meaning 'bestow, carry out' came later.
㐌 (looks like 也 plus a stroke) — traditionally the sound part (也 yě); today the match with shī is only a loose clue.

example.hanzi: 政府将从下个月开始实施新的环保政策。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ jiāng cóng xià gè yuè kāishǐ shíshī xīn de huánbǎo zhèngcè.
example.english: The government will implement new environmental policies starting next month.
example.fact: The Montreal Protocol, implemented in 1989 to phase out ozone-depleting chemicals such as CFCs, is widely regarded as one of the most successful international environmental treaties ever ratified. The ozone layer over Antarctica has been steadily recovering since, and scientists project it could fully heal by around 2066.

examples.hanzi: 这项规定从明年一月开始实施。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiàng guīdìng cóng míngnián yī yuè kāishǐ shíshī.
examples.english: This rule takes effect from January next year.

examples.hanzi: 学校正在实施新的教学办法。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zhèngzài shíshī xīn de jiàoxué bànfǎ.
examples.english: The school is implementing a new teaching method.

components.note: 予 (yǔ, give) is only a loose sound hint for shū; compare 序 xù and 预 yù.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 适 is to go to what suits you. 舌 is a simplification stand-in, not a real clue.

example.hanzi: 这张沙发又软又舒适，坐着看书很惬意。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhāng shāfā yòu ruǎn yòu shūshì, zuòzhe kànshū hěn qièyì.
example.english: This sofa is soft and comfortable — it's very pleasant to sit and read on it.
example.fact: Memory foam, now common in comfortable mattresses and sofa cushions, was originally developed by NASA in 1966 to cushion astronauts and pilots against the extreme g-forces of spaceflight. It only became widely available in home furniture in the 1990s.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒店的床非常舒适。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn de chuáng fēicháng shūshì.
examples.english: The beds in this hotel are very comfortable.

examples.hanzi: 他过着舒适的退休生活。
examples.pinyin: Tā guò zhe shūshì de tuìxiū shēnghuó.
examples.english: He leads a comfortable retired life.

components.note: 见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 这座古老的桥见证了这座城市数百年的历史。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔlǎo de qiáo jiànzhèngle zhè zuò chéngshì shùbǎi nián de lìshǐ.
example.english: This ancient bridge has witnessed hundreds of years of the city's history.
example.fact: The Charles Bridge in Prague, completed in 1402, has withstood floods, wars, and heavy daily use for over 600 years. A long-standing legend claims egg yolks were mixed into its mortar to strengthen it, though modern chemical analysis has found no clear evidence supporting the story.

examples.hanzi: 我们见证了这一历史时刻。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiànzhèng le zhè yí lìshǐ shíkè.
examples.english: We witnessed this historic moment.

examples.hanzi: 他在合同上作为见证人签了字。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hétong shàng zuòwéi jiànzhèngrén qiān le zì.
examples.english: He signed the contract as a witness.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 核 is a fruit stone or kernel; 木 marks trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 桌 table.
亥 (hài) is a loose sound clue; it also sounds out 孩 hái, 咳 ké and 刻 kè.

example.hanzi: 这个桃子的核很大。
example.pinyin: Zhège táozi de hé hěn dà.
example.english: This peach has a very big pit.
example.fact: 核 is a fruit pit, and also a nucleus or core: 核心 (core), 核桃 (walnut), 核实 (to verify). Because of the atomic nucleus, 核 now also means nuclear: 核电站, 核武器.

examples.hanzi: 吃完苹果别忘了把核扔掉。
examples.pinyin: Chī wán píngguǒ bié wàng le bǎ hé rēng diào.
examples.english: After eating the apple, don't forget to throw away the core.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司的核心产品卖得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī de héxīn chǎnpǐn mài de hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This company's core product sells very well.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.

example.hanzi: 大象是陆地上现存最大的动物。
example.pinyin: Dàxiàng shì lùdì shàng xiàncún zuì dà de dòngwù.
example.english: Elephants are the largest living land animals.
example.fact: African elephants can weigh up to 6,000 kilograms and are among the few animals confirmed to recognize themselves in a mirror, a sign of self-awareness they share with humans, great apes, and dolphins. They also appear to mourn their dead, sometimes returning to visit and touch the bones of deceased herd members.

examples.hanzi: 动物园里的大象正在洗澡。
examples.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ de dàxiàng zhèngzài xǐzǎo.
examples.english: The elephants in the zoo are taking a bath.

examples.hanzi: 大象的鼻子又长又灵活。
examples.pinyin: Dàxiàng de bízi yòu cháng yòu línghuó.
examples.english: An elephant's trunk is long and flexible.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魂, 魅, 愧; 魔 is a demon.
麻 (má) is a near sound match for mó; also in 磨 mó and 摩 mó.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 这个古老的传说讲述了一把拥有魔力的剑。
example.pinyin: Zhège gǔlǎo de chuánshuō jiǎngshùle yì bǎ yǒngyǒu mólì de jiàn.
example.english: This ancient legend tells of a sword with magic power.
example.fact: The legend of Excalibur, King Arthur's magical sword, has roots in Welsh and Breton Celtic mythology. The earliest known written account of a sword given by a supernatural power appears in Geoffrey of Monmouth's 12th-century chronicle Historia Regum Britanniae, long before the more familiar 'Lady of the Lake' version of the story took shape.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的魔力让孩子们着迷。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de mólì ràng háizimen zháomí.
examples.english: The magic in the story fascinates the children.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌好像有一种魔力。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē hǎoxiàng yǒu yì zhǒng mólì.
examples.english: This song seems to have a kind of magic.

components.note: 页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.
疒 (illness) — marks sickness and pain, as in 病, 痛, 疗; 疼 is to ache.
冬 (dōng) hints at the sound: 疼 téng is close.

example.hanzi: 他昨晚没睡好,今天头疼。
example.pinyin: tā zuówǎn méi shuìhǎo, jīntiān tóuténg.
example.english: He didn't sleep well last night, so today he has a headache.
example.fact: Willow bark, rich in a compound called salicin, was used for pain relief in ancient Egypt and Greece thousands of years before modern medicine existed. In 1897, Bayer chemist Felix Hoffmann synthesized a more stable version of the active compound, giving the world aspirin — still one of the most widely used pain relievers today.

examples.hanzi: 我今天头疼，不想出门。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān tóuténg, bù xiǎng chūmén.
examples.english: I have a headache today and don't want to go out.

examples.hanzi: 这道数学题让我很头疼。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào shùxué tí ràng wǒ hěn tóuténg.
examples.english: This math problem is giving me a headache.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.
宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家, 安, 室; 宴 is a feast at home.
妟 (yàn) gives the sound exactly: 宴 yàn.

example.hanzi: 公司为客户举办了一场豪华晚宴。
example.pinyin: gōngsī wèi kèhù jǔbànle yī chǎng háohuá wǎnyàn.
example.english: The company held a lavish banquet for its clients.
example.fact: The Field of the Cloth of Gold in 1520 was a diplomatic summit between England's Henry VIII and France's Francis I, built around weeks of jousting, feasting, and banquets so extravagant that they nearly bankrupted both royal treasuries. Despite the spectacle, the two kings failed to form a lasting alliance and were at war with each other again within a few years.

examples.hanzi: 今晚的晚宴在八点开始。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn de wǎnyàn zài bā diǎn kāishǐ.
examples.english: Tonight's banquet starts at eight.

examples.hanzi: 他们在酒店里举办了结婚晚宴。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài jiǔdiàn lǐ jǔbàn le jiéhūn wǎnyàn.
examples.english: They held their wedding banquet at the hotel.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — value and price, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy, 费 fee.
矢 (arrow) with a flag 方: a clan or troop gathered under its banner, with arrows at hand.

example.hanzi: 这座城堡曾经属于一位贵族。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò chéngbǎo céngjīng shǔyú yī wèi guìzú.
example.english: This castle once belonged to a nobleman.
example.fact: The Domesday Book, compiled in 1086 on the orders of William the Conqueror, catalogued nearly every landholding in England so the new Norman nobility could be taxed accurately. It remains one of the oldest and most detailed public administrative records in European history, and historians still consult it today.

examples.hanzi: 他出身于一个贵族家庭。
examples.pinyin: Tā chūshēn yú yí ge guìzú jiātíng.
examples.english: He was born into an aristocratic family.

examples.hanzi: 贵族们常常在宫殿里举行舞会。
examples.pinyin: Guìzúmen chángcháng zài gōngdiàn lǐ jǔxíng wǔhuì.
examples.english: Nobles often held balls in the palace.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 呜 imitates sobbing or a whistle.
乌 (wū) — same sound: 呜 wū. 乌 means crow.

example.hanzi: 小狗在门口呜呜地叫。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu zài ménkǒu wūwū de jiào.
example.english: The puppy is whimpering at the door.
example.fact: 呜呜 imitates sobbing, whimpering, or a siren or train whistle. Texters use 呜呜呜 for cute crying. 呜呼 is an old exclamation of grief, and 一命呜呼 jokingly means "to kick the bucket."

examples.hanzi: 火车呜的一声开走了。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē wū de yì shēng kāi zǒu le.
examples.english: The train pulled away with a whoo.

examples.hanzi: 她呜呜地哭了起来。
examples.pinyin: Tā wūwū de kū le qǐlái.
examples.english: She started sobbing.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — a family: 原 origin, 压 press, 厅 hall. 厚 originally meant a thick mound or hill, hence 'thick, deep' (厚度 thickness).
日 (sun) — together with 子 (child) in the inner part. Dictionary story: sunlight and children in a house; a memory aid, not proven.

example.hanzi: 外面很冷，你多穿一件厚衣服。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, nǐ duō chuān yí jiàn hòu yīfu.
example.english: It is cold outside, so wear a thicker coat.
example.fact: 厚 is the opposite of 薄 (báo). It describes thickness of flat things like books or coats, and figuratively generosity: 厚道 (honest and kind), 厚礼 (a generous gift). 厚脸皮 means thick-skinned or shameless.

examples.hanzi: 这本字典很厚，我带不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn zìdiǎn hěn hòu, wǒ dài bu dòng.
examples.english: This book is very thick, and I read it for a month.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你对我这么厚爱。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ duì wǒ zhème hòu'ài.
examples.english: Thank you for being so kind to me.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks slopes and barriers, as in 院, 阶, 障; 防 is a dike to guard against floods, then to defend.
方 (fāng) gives the sound: 防 fáng is close, as in 房 fáng and 妨 fáng.
萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.

example.hanzi: 出门前带把伞,以防万一下雨。
example.pinyin: chūmén qián dài bǎ sǎn, yǐfángwànyī xiàyǔ.
example.english: Bring an umbrella before going out, just in case it rains.
example.fact: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault, carved into a mountainside on a remote Norwegian island, stores duplicate seed samples from gene banks around the world as insurance against war, disease, or climate disaster. Built to withstand earthquakes and rising sea levels, it currently holds well over a million seed samples, all kept just in case.

examples.hanzi: 多带点钱吧，以防万一。
examples.pinyin: Duō dài diǎn qián ba, yǐfángwànyī.
examples.english: Bring a bit more money, just in case.

examples.hanzi: 以防万一，我已经备份了文件。
examples.pinyin: Yǐfángwànyī, wǒ yǐjīng bèifèn le wénjiàn.
examples.english: Just in case, I've already backed up the files.
